title: Candidate pattern: one-way quality ratchets and documentation gates
summary: Baseline existing debt, reject regressions, automatically bank improvements, require explicit review for threshold increases, and verify documentation claims against executable repository facts.
incompatible_when: The metric is unstable, easy to game, or disconnected from a meaningful engineering outcome.
procedure: Choose a measurable signal and document whether it is blocking or advisory.
Freeze current debt as a reviewed baseline and fail only on regression.
Make baseline reductions automatic or routine, but require explicit review to raise a cap.
Keep exception lists visible and shrink-only.
Add documentation gates for counts, commands, routes, versions, and other machine-checkable claims.
verification: Prove a regression fails, a neutral change passes, and an improvement shrinks or can safely update the baseline.
Verify the CI workflow runs the ratchet and documentation checks on the intended event paths.
rollback: Return a noisy metric to advisory status with a tracked repair plan; retain the previous baseline and evidence.

confidence.rationale: The repository documents mature ratchet mechanics and CI ownership, but promotion requires successful reuse.
